text:
laura: hitting a surprising auth issue in python SDK when running multiple clients and rotating API keys via env in a long-lived process.
ishaan: sync or async? tiny repro pls.
laura: async. minimal repro: set REDWOOD_API_KEY=K_A; client_a = AsyncRedwoodClient(); later rotate env to K_B; client_a still sends K_A on requests.
maria: did you pass api_key into constructor or rely on env?
laura: env only. new client_b created after rotation usually picks K_B but timing is flaky.
ishaan: sounds like the env-backed provider caches at init or there's a global singleton.
ben: workaround: inject a small per-client provider that reads os.getenv every call. example: class EnvProvider: def get(): return os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY') then AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key_provider=EnvProvider()).
maria: propose changes: (1) expose an AuthProvider Protocol for typing; (2) add api_key_provider param; (3) add env_read_strategy flag ("cached"|"per_call") defaulting to "cached" for perf; (4) add client.reload_credentials() to force refresh.
ishaan: agree. add tests: two clients in same process with different envs over time, and concurrent init to catch race. also perf microbenchmark for per-call getenv.
laura: filed issue with repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/948 (labels: bug, auth, regression).
sdk-bot: Routing to #eng-sdks (ticket: SDK-948).
ben: will draft PR that introduces AuthProvider Protocol and api_key_provider, keep backwards compat, add docs snippet under "Credential rotation in long-lived processes".
maria: docs should include typed examples for mypy and an explicit recipe for sidecars.
laura: thanks all, saving this thread for future hunters. :coffee:
